run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p', run a `range: { "@timestamp": { gte: "2026-06-03T00:00:00" } }` query filtered to level=ERROR and tell me the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: The requested query against index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p returned a count of 0, but not because there are no ERROR logs: the index has no @timestamp field at all. Its mapping contains only ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text), i.e. no date-typed field, so the tool applied no time filter (time_filter.applied=false) and the range clause on the non-existent @timestamp matched nothing. Re-running with the field that actually holds the log time, ingest_ts, gives 7 ERROR documents at or after 2026-06-03T00:00:00 (ingest_ts 2026-06-03T08:01:00 through 08:07:00). Without any time range the index holds 12 ERROR documents out of 16 total; the remaining 5 ERROR documents are dated 2026-06-02T08:01:00–08:05:00 and the 4 INFO documents 2026-06-03T09:01:00–09:04:00. Two caveats: ingest_ts is mapped as keyword, so the range comparison is lexicographic on the stored ISO-8601 strings (it orders correctly for the values observed, but it is not a date-type range), and naming ingest_ts as time_field was ignored by the tool because no date field is mapped. All 16 documents are dated June 2026, i.e. outside the authorized window (2026-10-24T18:12:30Z–2026-11-23T18:12:30Z), so they cannot be tied to that window; counts describe the index as queried, not the incident window.

claims.text: The mapping of index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p has exactly three properties: ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text). There is no @timestamp property and no date-typed property.
At query time the index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p held 16 documents (docs.count 16, health green, status open).

The exact requested query — bool(term level=ERROR, range @timestamp gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00) with size 0 — returned total.value 0 (relation eq), timed_out false, shards failed 0, with time_filter {"applied":false,"field":null} and the note that no matched index maps a date field.
Corrected to the field that actually carries the log time, the query bool(term level=ERROR, range ingest_ts gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00) returned total.value 7.

The 7 ERROR documents dated at or after 2026-06-03T00:00:00 have ingest_ts 2026-06-03T08:01:00, 08:02:00, 08:03:00, 08:04:00, 08:05:00, 08:06:00 and 08:07:00, with messages 'err today 1' through 'err today 7'.

Documents with ingest_ts before 2026-06-03T00:00:00 number 5, all level ERROR, at 2026-06-02T08:01:00 through 08:05:00 (messages 'err yest 1'–'err yest 5'); together with the 7 later ERROR documents this accounts for all 12 ERROR documents in the index.
Without any time filter, level=ERROR totals 12 documents in app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p, and the index totals 16 documents.
Aggregating all documents with ingest_ts >= 2026-06-03T00:00:00 by the level keyword gives 7 ERROR and 4 INFO (total 11); the 4 INFO documents carry ingest_ts 2026-06-03T09:01:00–09:04:00.

Passing time_field "ingest_ts" to the search was ignored — the result notes 'time_field ingest_ts was ignored: no matched index maps any date field' — and the unfiltered level=ERROR count stayed 12 with time_filter.applied false.
All observed documents are dated June 2026 (2026-06-02T08:01:00 through 2026-06-03T09:04:00), which lies entirely outside the authorized window 2026-10-24T18:12:30Z to 2026-11-23T18:12:30Z.

The zero from the requested query is a field-name artifact, not an absence of ERROR logs: because @timestamp is unmapped, the range clause and any date-based time filter can never match or restrict documents in this index, and the same query written against ingest_ts returns 7.

Against reading the 7 as a clean date-type count: ingest_ts is mapped as keyword, so range on it is a lexicographic string comparison. It ordered these ISO-8601, timezone-less values chronologically, but a differently formatted or offset timestamp string in the same field would not necessarily be ordered or compared as a date.

Treat the correct answers as: 0 for the literal @timestamp query (no such field), 7 for level=ERROR with ingest_ts >= 2026-06-03T00:00:00, and 12 for level=ERROR with no time filter. If this index is to be time-filtered properly, index a date-typed field (for example @timestamp or make ingest_ts a date) rather than relying on keyword string ordering.

gaps: Index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p has no date-typed field, so no Elasticsearch-side window filtering was possible (time_filter.applied=false on every query); the ingest_ts ranges above are explicit query filters over a keyword field, not tool-applied time filtering.

All 16 documents observed are dated June 2026 and lie outside the authorized window (2026-10-24T18:12:30Z–2026-11-23T18:12:30Z), so nothing here describes the incident window; counts describe the index at query time only.

Whether ingest_ts values always use the same 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' format (needed for lexicographic range to equal chronological ordering) was only checked for the 16 documents returned, not for the whole retention period.
Change history is not a configured integration in this Run, so who changed the index mapping or its date-field configuration is unknown.
next_steps: Confirm with the log-shipper/index-template owner whether app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p is supposed to carry a date-typed @timestamp, and reindex or add a date template field if date-based queries are required.
If incident-window log analysis is needed, identify whether a separate index or field holds 2026-10/2026-11 logs, since this index holds only June 2026 documents.
